A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlowAlign. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite the rewritten theoretical formulation and changed pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-editing comparisons, backward-editing measurements, runtime results, a 25-participant preference study, and qualitative video and 3D editing results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the quantitative comparisons and the human study with 505 responses.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 substantially changes the proposed optimal-control loss: v1 combines a running flow-matching penalty with a target-image endpoint loss, whereas v3 uses source-image similarity at the endpoint with finite eta. Algorithms 1 and 3 retain identical discrete editing updates, so this loss reformulation does not establish a changed implementation or rerun.

E1.justification: Both retain PIEBench evaluation, EditBench/PIEBench examples, backward editing, DAVIS video editing, and Gaussian-splatting experiments using IN2N and PDS scenes. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The image-editing comparisons retain SDEdit, DDIB, RF-inversion, and FlowEdit. The 3D comparison retains SDS, DDS, PDS, and IGS2GS, including the same stated backbone adaptations.

E3.justification: The stated image-evaluation budgets, CFG sweep, metrics, 700-image pool, human-study design, and 50-case runtime evaluation are unchanged. Removed 3D hyperparameter disclosures do not establish that the experimental settings changed.

E4.justification: The backward-editing consistency analysis, omega/zeta ablations in Figures 6 and 11, runtime analysis, and qualitative application examples are retained. No new analysis tests the revised terminal-point formulation.

E5.justification: Both retain the same aggregate preference ratios and runtime averaging practices. Neither adds repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain all numerical entries, including FlowAlign's backward-editing PSNR of 27.42, PIEBench background PSNR of 25.50, and runtime of 7.14 seconds. Quantitative plots and qualitative result panels are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix A replace the optimal-control problem, Lemma 1, and Proposition 1's derivation. The eta-to-zero argument and coefficient lambda_t/((1+lambda_t)t) are replaced by a source-terminal formulation with gamma = -eta/(1-eta*t). The new proof explicitly introduces a first-order approximation of the remaining velocity integral.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction redefine the central contribution from flow-matching regularization to terminal-point source-similarity regularization. Claims concerning source preservation, editing quality, efficiency, and reverse editing remain, while the conclusion is only partly updated to the new formulation.

C2.justification: The central mechanism explanation changes from a running flow-matching penalty to endpoint similarity enforcing consistency along the trajectory. v3 newly argues that finite eta avoids a trivial identity solution. Existing interpretations of empirical results and limitations concerning inference cost, model bias, and video temporal inconsistency remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F.2 removes the 3D settings lambda_t = 30 sigma_t^2, sigma_t = t, the 0.9-to-0.1 time range, and step size eta_t = 1 + 30 sigma_t^2 without replacement values. Algorithm 2 also drops the step-size input while still using it. Other implementation details and the promised code-access location remain.

R1.justification: The same cited works are retained. v3 adds a specific positioning argument contrasting its finite terminal-penalty weight with RF-inversion's stated eta-to-infinity limit, and emphasizes this relationship in its optimal-control motivation.

P1.justification: The section hierarchy and most experimental and supplementary prose remain intact. Targeted narrative revisions accompany the new formulation, Section 3.3 is renamed, citations become numerical, and the author block adds Jonghyun Park and removes the equal-contribution note.

P2.justification: The figure panels and table membership are retained. Figure 2 moves and receives a revised explanatory caption; Table 1 becomes a larger standalone display instead of a small text-wrapped table; Figure 6 moves alongside the ablation discussion. Other differences mainly concern reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the source-preservation objective explicit and acknowledges a first-order approximation, but the theoretical benefit is unresolved: its new gamma has an unexplained pole at t = 1/eta for eta > 1, despite the claimed positive regularization. Several passages still describe the removed flow-matching penalty, and Appendix F.2 loses reproducibility settings. These concerns coexist with clearer exposition and Table 1 presentation, while empirical evidence is unchanged, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
